title: The Impact of Qubit Connectivity on Quantum Advantage in Noisy IQP Circuits
summary: Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-time (IQP) circuits are a candidate for demonstrating near-term quantum advantage, as their sampling task is believed to be classically hard in the ideal theoretical setting under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions. In noisy implementations, however, this hardness can disappear once circuit depth exceeds a noise-dependent critical threshold. We show that qubit connectivity is a key parameter in this transition, since sparse architectures require additional routing to implement long-range interactions, thereby increasing compiled circuit depth.
